711403.lxx: in LXX for מוֹט, זוּעַ, etc.
711403.full: σαλεύω (σάλος), [in LXX for מוֹט, זוּעַ, etc. ;] prop., of the action of wind, storm, etc., to agitate, shake: of a reed, Mat.11:7, Luk.7:24; a house, Luk.6:48, Act.4:31 16:26; the earth, Heb.12:26; the heavenly bodies, Mat.24:29, Mrk.13:25, Luk.21:26; of a vessel shaken in filling, Luk.6:38. Metaphorical, __(a) to shake, i.e. to render insecure: τὰ σαλευόμενα, τὰ μὴ., Heb.12:27; __(b) with accusative of person(s), to cast down from a sense of security and happiness: Act.2:25 (LXX); __(with) to unsettle or drive away: pass., before ἀπὸ τ. νοός, 2Th.2:2; __(d) to stir up: τ. ὄχλους, Act.17:13.† (AS)

711419.full: Σαλμών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שַׂלְמוֹן), Salmon: Mat.1:4-5, Luk.3:32 (Σαλά, WH, R, mg.).† (AS)

711420.full: σάλος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for מוֹט, etc. ;] in poets and late prose, a tossing, as of an earthquake; esp. the tossing, the rolling swell of the sea: Luk.21:25.† (AS)

s: a trumpet, used in war and in religious ceremonies
711424.lxx: in LXX chiefly for שׁוֹפָר, חֲצֹצְרָה
711424.full: σάλπιγξ, -ιγγος, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for שׁוֹפָר, חֲצֹצְרָה ;] a trumpet, used in war and in religious ceremonies: 1Co.14:8, Heb.12:19, Rev.1:10 4:1 8:2, 6 8:11 9:14 By meton., a trumpet blast: μετὰ σ. μεγάλης, Mat.24:31; ἐν σ. θεοῦ, 1Th.4:16; ἐν τ. ἐσχάτῃ σ., 1Co.15:52.† (AS)

711425.full: σαλπίζω [in LXX chiefly for תָּקַע ;] to sound a trumpet: Rev.8:6 ff. Rev.9:1, 13 10:7 11:15; metaphorically, Mat.6:2. Impers., the trumpet sounds: 1Co.15:52.† (AS)

711430.full: Σολομών, -ῶνος (so prop., but Rec. has frequently -ῶν, -ῶντος, as also WH in Act.3:11 5:12; in Act.7:47 T has Σαλωμών, as LXX freq., indecl.; see B1., § 10, 1; Tdf., Prol., 104, 119; WH, App., 158), ὁ (Heb. שְׁלֹמֹה), Solomon: Mat.1:6-7 6:29 12:42, Luk.11:31 12:27, Jhn.10:23, Act.3:11 5:12 7:47.† (AS)

711431.full: Σολομών, -ῶνος (so prop., but Rec. has frequently -ῶν, -ῶντος, as also WH in Act.3:11 5:12; in Act.7:47 T has Σαλωμών, as LXX freq., indecl.; see B1., § 10, 1; Tdf., Prol., 104, 119; WH, App., 158), ὁ (Heb. שְׁלֹמֹה), Solomon: Mat.1:6-7 6:29 12:42, Luk.11:31 12:27, Jhn.10:23, Act.3:11 5:12 7:47.† (AS)

711436.full: Σαμαε Samae - a name found only in LXX at 2Sa.5.16 with no equivalent in the Hebrew text

711449.full: Σαμαρία (Rec. -άρεια), -ας, ἡ (Heb. שֹׁמְרוֹן; Aram. שָׁמְרַיִן), Samaria; __(a) the city: Act.8:5 (and perhaps also Act.8:9, 14); __(b) the region: Luk.17:11, Jhn.4:4-5, 7, Act.1:8 8:1 (and perhaps also Act.8:9, 14) Act.9:31 15:3.† (AS)

711450.full: Σαμαρείτης (-ίτης, Τ; see WH, App., 154; BI., § 3, 4), -ον, ό, a Samaritan, i.e. an inhabitant of the city or the region of Samaria, in NT always the latter (see: Σαμαρία): Mat.10:5, Luk.9:52 10:33 17:16, Jhn.4:9, 39-40, Act.8:25; as an opprobrious epithet, Jhn.8:48.† (AS)

711451.full: Σαμαρεῖτις (-ῖτις, T, see supr.), -ιδος, ἡ __1. in FlJ (B.J., i, 21, 2, al.), the region of Samaria. __2. a Samaritan woman: Jhn.4:9.† (AS)

711458.full: 1. a triangular musical instrument with four strings , Lat. sambuca, (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. an engine of like form used in sieges, (Plutarch) (ML)

s: Samos, an island in the Ægean
711470.full: Σάμος, -ου, ἡ Samos, an island in the Ægean: Act.20:15.† (AS)

711473.full: Σαμουήλ, ὁ indecl. (in FlJ, Σαμούηλος; Heb. שְׁמוּאֵל), Samuel (1Ki.1:20, al.): Act.3:24 13:20, Heb.11:32.† (AS)

711480.full: Samekh, the 15th letter of the Hebrew alphabet; used in LXX for acrostic Psalms such as Psa.119

711482.full: Σαμψών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שִׁמְשׁוֹן), Samson (Jdg.13:1-25 ff.): Heb.11:32.† (AS)

711488.lxx: in LXX: Jos.9:5, Isa.20:2 (נָעַל, elsewhere rendered ὑπόδημα, which see), Jdth.10:4 16:9 *
711488.full: σανδάλιον, -ου, τό (dimin. of σάνδαλον, prob. Persian), [in LXX: Jos.9:5, Isa.20:2 (נָעַל, elsewhere rendered ὑπόδημα, which see), Jdth.10:4 16:9 * ;] a sandal: Mrk.6:9, Act.12:8.† (AS)

711499.full: Σαούλ, ὁ indecl. (in FlJ, Σάουλος; Heb. שָׁאוּל) Saul; __(a) the King of Israel: Act.13:21; __(b) the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul, used in the indecl. form only in address (cf. Σαῦλος): Act.9:4, 17 22:7, 13 26:14.† (AS)
